summary: Yong Hua is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries, and founded Triten Norbutse and Menri monasteries. He served as lopön at Menri and held visiting scholar posts at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche (born 1975) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Sherab Ling Monastery and the Dzongsar Institute (~1994–1997) under several traditional teachers, and became abbot of Sherab Ling Monastery around 1998.
Yongshan He is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at McMaster University under James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang (1893–1964) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Tsinghua and Harvard, he held professorships at Southeast, National Central, and National Southwestern Associated universities, and served as professor and vice-president at Peking University.

Yongyu Chen works in Buddhist studies and other fields. Chen studied at Cornell University (BA) and Harvard University (PhD student), held a professorship at Joong-Ang Sangha University (attested 2015), and served as an ArtTable Fellow at Public Art Fund in 2025.

Yonten Gyatso (1933–2002) worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he later served as research advisor for Tibetan Studies.

Yoshifumi Honjo (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology educated at Kyoto University. His career includes faculty positions at Kobe Women's University (1989–2004), Otani University, and Bukkyo University, where he served as professor of Buddhism in 2014.

Yoshifumi Mizuno (born 1958) is an Indology and linguistics scholar. After studying at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the University of Tokyo and served as associate professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (2000–2024).

Yoshihide Yoshizu (1943–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who earned his doctorate at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata and Shoson Miyamoto. He taught at Komazawa University from 1971, becoming professor in 2001, and researched at the University of Virginia (1985).

Yoshihiko Amino (1929–2004) was a Japanese historian who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1950). He held academic posts at Nagoya University (~1967–1980) and Kanagawa University (~1980–1999).
Yoshihiko Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007) and held leadership positions at Kongojushinkai and Kongozyu (attested 2017).

Yoshihiko Sakurai is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies and served as a part-time lecturer (attested 2003) at Ryukoku University. He has also worked as a researcher at the Jodo Shinshu Hongwanji-ha Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Center.
Yoshihiro Hayashi specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2009, he has served as a professor at Ritsumeikan University and as a part-time lecturer at Shitennoji University.
Yoshihiro Matsunami (born 1935) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a professorship at Taisho University (attested 1991–1999) and served as the university's president in 2001.

Yoshihito Muroji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He has held positions at Kyoto University, Koyasan University (1995–2012), and Shiga University of Medical Science (2014–2015).
Yoshiki Motoaki works in Buddhist studies and has held affiliations with Otani University (attested 2013) and the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Yoshimi Nozawa is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who has served as a part-time lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yoshinobu Kimoto (born 1950) is a historian of Japan educated at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. He held academic posts at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College, served as president of Koshien Junior College (2000–2012), and was a professor at Ryukoku University (2013–2021).

Yoshinobu Sakade (1934–2020) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1953–1957) under Mitsuji Fukunaga and served on the faculty at Kansai University from approximately 1977 to 2005.
